ja: יראתו על פניכם לבלתי תחטאו, וקאלוא אואילנא ע"ס הסתכל בשלשה דברים ואין אתה בא לידי עברה, דע מאין באת, ולאן אתה הולך, ולפני מי אתה עתיד ליתן דין וחשבון. מאין באת מטפה סרוחה, ולאן אתה הולך למקום עפר רמה ותולעה, ולפני מי אתה עתיד ליתן דין וחשבון לפני מלך מלכי המלכים הקדוש ברוך הוא. פצל. ו. ואמא אלסירה אלתי ינבגי אן יכון עליהא צאחב אלתואצ'ע פעשרה כ'לאל. אולהא, אלעלם באללה ג'ל ועז ובצפאתה אלחסני, ומא פצ'ל בה אלאנסאן עלי סאיר אלחיואן, כקולה תמשילהו במעשי ידיך כל שתה תחת רגליו. פאד'א מייז ען ג'לאלהֵ עט'מהֵ אלכ'אלק ותסאני קדרתה ועאלי חכמתה תואצ'ע לה ותד'לל בין ידיה, קיאסא במא אוצי בה אלחכים אל תתהדר לפני מלך ולפני גדולים אל תעמוד, ואחרי ואוכד מלך אלמלוך וסייד אלסאדאת תעאלי ען אלתשביה ואלתמת'יל, כמא קאלת חנה ע"ס אין קדוש כה' ואין צור כאלהינו. ואלת'אניה אלעלם בלואזם אלשריעה ואלעקל עליה, ותלאוהֵ כתאב אללה, ואלוקוף עלי אלעלם אלמעקול ואלמכתוב ואלמנקול ליסתמד בהא ומנהא שרוט אלתואצ'ע ומואצ'ע אסתעמאלה. ואלת'אלת'ה סעהֵ אלאכ'לאק ואלצבר עלי מא יכרה מן אלקול ואלפעל ללה תעאלי, כמא קאל אם גמלתי שולמי רע ואחלצה צררי
en_candidate:
That comes about by attending in thought and turning the inward attention to seven things.

**The first**: the root of his coming-to-be and the beginning of his origin from semen and blood, after their decay and the foulness of their odor; then his nourishment by the blood of menses for the duration of his being in the belly of his mother; then his coming forth in a state of weakness, of frailty of body and limb; then his ascent from this rank to the next, until he reaches his maturity; then his taking-up into old age, until the conclusion of his term. One of the sages said in this concept: "I marvel at one who passes urine through the channel of urination twice — how he is proud and tilts his nose." Reflection on this and on its like of the human's affair makes humility binding upon him; for this reason the Friend (peace be upon him) said: "Lord, what is the human, that You take note of him; the son of man, that You give thought to him?" (Psalms 144:3); and he said: "Man born of woman is short of days and full of agitation" (Job 14:1); and he said: "But I am a worm and not a man" (Psalms 22:7); and he said: "How much less, then, man — a worm — and the son of man — a maggot" (Job 25:6).

**The second**: when he reflects on the magnitude of what has met him in this world of the kinds of trial — by hunger, thirst, heat, cold, sicknesses, calamities, and anxieties from which he has no rest except by death — and when the discerning man has gathered all of this and become sharp to his weakness and the slightness of his perception of what would ward this off from his soul, he discriminates from the picture of his standing that he is like a captive in this abode (rather, he is so in true reality); and he humbles himself with the humility of the imprisoned captive who has no contrivance and no power for the freeing of his soul without the satisfaction of his master with him, as He said: "Let the groan of the captive come before You" (Psalms 79:11); and: "Bring my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks to Your name" (Psalms 142:8).

**The third**: when he reflects on the conclusion of his term and the swiftness of the descent of death upon him; the cutting-off of his hope and his expectation at that; his abandonment of his affairs and his despair of provisioning himself with anything from them or benefiting by them; the picture of his standing in the grave — the light of his face having gone, his color blackened, the worms and the rot and the pus having fallen upon him, the traces of the beauties of his body departed, the foulness of his odor intensified as if he had never been bathed nor cleaned nor scented with the like of perfumes. When the like of this and its likes has occurred to the human's mind, he humbles himself within himself; he is lowered; he is not conceited, does not tower, no vanity or pride enters him — as Scripture said: "Cease from man, in whose nostril is breath; for in what is he to be reckoned?" (Isaiah 2:22); and He said: "Surely the children of man are vapor; the children of men are a lie" (Psalms 62:10).
